message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have a dedicated tool that can pull up‑to‑date holiday calendars from an external source. However, based on the publicly available information for 2023, here’s a list of the most common long weekends that Canadians usually enjoy:

| Date(s) | Holiday | Typical Long Weekend |
|---------|---------|----------------------|
| **January 1** (Sunday) | New Year’s Day | Jan 1–3 (New Year’s Eve & New Year’s Day) |
| **February 20** (Monday) | Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, etc.) | Feb 18–20 |
| **April 7** (Friday) | Good Friday | Apr 7–9 |
| **May 22** (Monday) | Victoria Day | May 20–22 |
| **July 1** (Saturday) | Canada Day | Jun 30–Jul 2 |
| **September 4** (Monday) | Labour Day | Sep 2–4 |
| **October 9** (Monday) | Thanksgiving | Oct 7–9 |
| **November 11** (Thursday) | Remembrance Day | Nov 10–12 |
| **December 25** (Monday) | Christmas Day | Dec 23–25 |

> **Note:**  
> • Some provinces observe different dates for certain holidays (e.g., Family Day is on February 20 in Ontario but on February 27 in Alberta).  
> • If you’re looking for a comprehensive, province‑specific list, you may want to consult the official government website or a reliable calendar service that provides holiday data for each province.

If you’d like me to calculate something else—like the total number of days off or the exact dates for a specific province—I can help with that using the `add` or `multiply` functions. Just let me know!
